solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Exercises that could lead to 'bio-scare'

indicators.note: could lead to says these letters, once rearranged, produce the word sought (a loose signal for reworking them)

explanation.surface: A fitness craze that might set off a health panic.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the eight letters of BIO-SCARE. The blogger called 'could lead to' a rather lame anagram signal, but it does say one set of letters turns into the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobic workouts are a familiar form of rhythmic fitness training, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Dispatch car crashing in Italy unfortunately

indicators.note: in places the jumbled car inside the jumbled country
unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the country's letters are rearranged
crashing smashes the word car into a new order

explanation.surface: A car wreck in Italy sadly calls for speed.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagram signals: 'crashing' works on the vehicle and 'unfortunately' on the country, and 'in' nests one result inside the other. 'Dispatch' looks like sending, but here it means speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispatch in the sense of speedy promptness is eager quickness, which alacrity also means.

clue.text: Area overrun by fire almost

indicators.note: overrun by says the answer lies spread inside the words that follow, swamped by them

explanation.surface: A district almost engulfed by flames.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a field or domain of activity, so it can stand for an area of interest.

clue.text: Commissions checks under the leadership of British engineers

indicators.note: under the leadership of puts the checks after, led by, the earlier pieces

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
to vet is to check thoroughly

explanation.surface: Army engineers inspecting appointments under British command.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A brevet was a military commission giving an officer a higher rank without extra pay.

clue.text: Revolutionary food originally provided by one in the kitchen

parts.note: Che Guevara was the famous Argentine revolutionary

indicators.note: originally picks the opening letter of the word food

explanation.surface: A rebel leader has a meal cooked for him.
explanation.definitionFit: A head cook working in a restaurant is a person found in the kitchen.

clue.text: One of the Channel Islands has a sort of appeal for loner

parts.note: Herm is a small island among the Channel Islands, near Guernsey
IT is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: An islander with a certain allure who keeps to himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Herm is a tiny car-free island near Guernsey, between Britain and France; 'a sort of appeal' is sex appeal, from the 1920s 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse living apart from society is a loner by another name.

clue.text: Bring out more when taken to court

indicators.note: when taken to means the court abbreviation is added to the end

parts.note: extra means more or additional

explanation.surface: Further evidence emerges in a legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to draw or pull something out, which bring out describes.

clue.text: One to put explosive charges in stratum at bottom of coal pit?

definitions.text: One to put explosive charges in

indicators.note: at bottom of says, in this down entry, the stratum word sits below the pit word

parts.note: a coal mine is a pit
a layer is a stratum

explanation.surface: A miner placing blasting charges in a seam at the foot of a colliery.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'at bottom of' puts the stratum beneath the pit. The surface pictures a miner blasting, but the definition is a ship that lays naval mines.
explanation.definitionFit: A minelayer is a ship or aircraft built to lay explosive mines at sea.

clue.text: One of the birds — only half of them hurry

indicators.note: only half of takes the front half of the word them

parts.note: rush means hurry

explanation.surface: Only half of the flock dashes off.
explanation.definitionFit: The thrush is a common songbird, one example of many bird species.

clue.text: Apprehension — peculiar sense following a military action

indicators.note: following tells us the jumbled piece comes after the earlier pieces

parts.note: war is military action on a large scale

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, so the word sense is to be reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier's uneasy feeling after a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiar' rearranges the word sense, and 'following' places that result after the battle. 'Apprehension' suggests fear, but here it means understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Apprehension in the sense of grasping or perceiving something is consciousness of it.

clue.text: Possibly a bit of grass son found on teacake

indicators.note: found on places the son letter before the teacake word

parts.note: a pikelet is a small thick griddle cake, like a crumpet, eaten at tea

explanation.surface: A boy is discovered sitting on a crumpet.
explanation.walkthrough: A PIKELET is a British teacake similar to a crumpet. 'Possibly' marks the definition as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A spikelet is the small flower cluster of grasses, so one may be part of a grass plant.

clue.text: Often organist is too much for this singer

indicators.note: is too much for says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An organist is often drowned out by a loud vocalist in the choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is too much for' is an unusual way to signal a hidden word: the run is literally more than the singer, overflowing across ofTEN ORganist.
explanation.definitionFit: This singer points to a male voice in the high register of a choir, one kind of vocalist.

clue.text: Being swindled makes a politician come in looking embarrassed

indicators.note: come in says the politician enters the middle of the colour word

parts.note: an embarrassed face turns red
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A conned MP blushes as he walks in.
explanation.definitionFit: To ramp is old slang for swindle or rob, so being swindled is being ramped.

clue.text: Car recovery folk in units along the road achieving wonders

indicators.note: in places the breakdown service inside the units of distance

parts.note: road distances in Britain are measured in miles
the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British breakdown service

explanation.surface: Breakdown crews covering great distances perform marvels.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC (Royal Automobile Club) is a British roadside breakdown service, like AAA in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Miracles are marvels beyond the ordinary, and wonders names the same amazing events.

clue.text: Bloke getting established after one fine display

indicators.note: after puts the established abbreviation behind the preceding letters

parts.note: a bloke is British slang for a man
I is the Roman numeral for one
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A man setting up a fine exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: To manifest something is to show it clearly, which is what display means as a verb.

clue.text: Party lanterns will get broken obviously

indicators.note: will get broken says the letters of the two fodder words are to be smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Paper lanterns at a party are bound to be smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a see-through manner means doing it plainly or evidently.

clue.text: A case is to get sorted out by fellow worker

indicators.note: get sorted out means to be put in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A legal case is resolved with help from a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: An associate is a partner or colleague, someone who works alongside you.

clue.text: A number stuck in poverty must be tidied up

indicators.note: stuck in says A and the number go inside the poverty word

parts.note: need is poverty or want
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Someone poor and stuck with a debt must sort things out.
explanation.definitionFit: To neaten is to make tidy, so neatened means tidied up in the past.

clue.text: Additional fee cheers e.g. vicar when in difficulties

indicators.note: when in difficulties means in trouble or disarray, so the fodder letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A churchman in trouble is cheered on by a congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder is CHEERS, EG and VICAR, thirteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant may add an extra charge for service to the bill, an additional fee.

clue.text: New edition produced by university in revamped series

indicators.note: in places the university letter inside the reworked word
revamped means remade, so the letters of series are rearranged

explanation.surface: A university press relaunches a revamped set of books.
explanation.definitionFit: A reissue is a fresh publication of something already issued, a new edition.

clue.text: Rope with which Henry gets cart pulled up

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of the name Henry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal

indicators.note: pulled up in a down entry means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a dray is a low heavy cart, as used by brewers

explanation.surface: Henry hauls his wagon uphill with a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled up' reverses DRAY to give YARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A halyard is a rope on a ship used for hoisting a sail or flag.

clue.text: Like some names following strict convention

definitions.meaning: names of particular people or places, such as London, are called nouns of this kind
correct and respectable in the conventional way

explanation.definitionFit: Names of specific people are proper nouns, and correct conventional behaviour is also so described.

clue.text: Flowing water runs around back of the church fence

indicators.note: runs around means the watercourse encircles the next pieces

parts.note: a river is a body of flowing water

indicators.note: back of picks the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A stream winds round behind a church to a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fence' looks like a boundary, but it is a dealer in stolen goods; 'runs around' wraps the watercourse round the last letter of 'the' and the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang a fence is someone who buys stolen goods, a receiver of them.

clue.text: Predicament requires gentle illumination

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play softly or gently
light is illumination

explanation.surface: A tricky situation calls for soft lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A plight is a difficult or unfortunate situation, which is what a predicament is.

clue.text: A ground prepared, but it's not right day for fertiliser

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the remaining letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Soil is readied, but today is the wrong day to spread manure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's not' removes R and D from A GROUND, leaving AGOUN, which 'prepared' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Guano is the droppings of seabirds or bats, used as a rich fertiliser.

clue.text: The female's last to receive present

parts.note: her is the female possessive, meaning the female's

indicators.note: last to picks the final letter of the word receive

explanation.surface: The woman is the final one to accept a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift; it means in attendance, as in answering a roll call.
explanation.definitionFit: Answering a roll call, a pupil says this word to mean in attendance.

clue.text: Famous 11 has power, with listeners hanging on

indicators.note: hanging on means the next piece is attached after the first letter

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
ears are what we listen with

explanation.surface: A celebrated singer commands an audience hanging on his every note.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Pears was the famous British singer, partner of the composer Benjamin Britten; 11 refers to the answer at 11-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pears is a well known example of a vocalist of the voice type described at clue 11.

clue.text: A benefit may follow the institution's end, on the other hand

indicators.note: may follow puts A and the benefit after the earlier pieces
end picks the last letter of the word that comes before it

parts.note: a gain is a benefit or advantage

explanation.surface: An organisation's closure might bring an advantage after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the institution's end' gives THE and N (the last letter of institution; the 's adds nothing).
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom used to introduce a contrasting thought, just like on the other hand.

clue.text: Tottered in the grass around lake with little energy

indicators.note: around says the grass word surrounds the next two letters

parts.note: a reed is a tall marsh grass
L is the map abbreviation for lake
E is the abbreviation for energy, a little of the word

explanation.surface: Someone stumbled through the reeds by a lake, feeling drained.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to stagger unsteadily, so reeled and tottered are synonyms in the past tense.

clue.text: US city personnel contributing nothing?

definitions.meaning: ... is a historic Wild West town in South Dakota
staff who add no value and could be cut from an organisation

explanation.walkthrough: The blogger noted it does not look like it, but this is a double definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Unproductive staff are called dead wood, and the name is also that of a South Dakota city.
